item.title: Gregor Mendel (1822–1884) — Failed Biology Exams, 28,000 Pea Plants in Brno, the Unread 1866 Paper, and the Abbot's Tax Rebellion
item.description: How a Silesian peasant's son funded by his younger sister's marriage dowry failed his Vienna biology teacher exams twice, studied experimental physics under Christian Doppler, quietly hand-pollinated 28,000 pea plants behind a Brno abbey wall to crack the discrete binomial algebra of heredity, read his 1865 paper to forty silent listeners, fell into Karl von Nägeli's apomictic hawkweed trap, waged a lonely ten-year Abbot's tax war, died unrecognized before his notebooks were burned, and launched modern genetics in 1900—closing with a One-Ångström journey inside Starch Branching Enzyme I (RCSB PDB 3AML and 7ML5) to watch the exact atomic mechanism behind Mendel's wrinkled peas.

item.title: James Clerk Maxwell & Emmy Noether (1831–1879 / 1882–1935) — Two Quiet Architects of Symmetry: Saturn's Rings, Displacement Current, Unpaid Göttingen Lectures, and Symmetry = Conservation
item.description: Two unassuming outsiders separated by half a century quietly erected the invisible mathematical girders of modern reality without ever chasing fame or titles. Follow Scottish boy 'Dafty' James Clerk Maxwell from pins-and-thread oval curves at fourteen, proving Saturn's rings are a vast swarm of independent particles, and surviving an abrupt Aberdeen university layoff to projecting the world's first color photograph, adding displacement current to deduce the speed of starlight from benchtop sparks and magnets, inventing Maxwell's Demon, and building Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory—alongside Bavarian algebraist Emmy Noether, who audited Erlangen lectures among 986 men, taught over a decade unpaid, untangled General Relativity's missing energy in Göttingen to prove that every continuous symmetry births an exact conservation law, rebuilt modern abstract algebra around Noetherian rings, calmly taught class field theory in her living room after the 1933 Nazi purge, and inspired Albert Einstein's glowing New York Times farewell from her Pennsylvania exile.

item.title: Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519) — Verrocchio's Workshop, Mirror-Script Dissections, Unfinished Masterpieces, and the Sforza Bronze Horse
item.description: Illegitimate son of a Florentine notary and a peasant orphan, excluded from Latin university schooling and scarred early by Florence's anonymous 1476 tamburo vice denunciation, Leonardo da Vinci pitched himself to Milanese warlord Ludovico Sforza as a weapons engineer—tacking painting onto the bottom of his ten-point letter as an afterthought. Follow his relentless visual obsessions across seventeen Milanese years of flaking dry-wall paint on The Last Supper and the doomed seventy-ton clay Gran Cavallo, eight chilling months drawing the revolutionary bird's-eye Imola map for Cesare Borgia, his searing street clash with Michelangelo, the undelivered Mona Lisa, candlelit hospital dissections unveiling coronary atherosclerosis and glass-cast aortic-valve sinus vortices validated four and a half centuries later, and his peaceful refuge at Francis I's Clos Lucé before heirs scattered over thirteen thousand unpublished mirror-script pages for three centuries.

item.title: William Harvey (1578–1657) — Padua's Anatomy Theater, Venous Valves, the 1628 Stroke-Volume Proof, and Civil-War Exile
item.description: From Elizabethan Folkestone and the dark walnut galleries of Padua's 1594 anatomical theater to twelve cautious years of eel vivisections and forearm ligatures at St. Bartholomew's Hospital, follow short, dagger-wearing royal physician William Harvey as he unleashes the 1628 Frankfurt quarto De Motu Cordis and its devastating Chapter IX stroke-volume proof—surviving a collapsed London practice, exonerating the 1634 Lancashire witches, reading calmly beneath a hedge as cannonballs strike at Edgehill, enduring the Parliamentary burning of his Whitehall manuscripts, answering Paris's Jean Riolan, and leaving one missing microscopic link closed four years after his death by Marcello Malpighi's 1661 frog-lung lens, followed by a One-Ångström molecular epilogue inside deoxyhemoglobin (PDB 2HHB) and oxyhemoglobin (PDB 1HHO).

item.title: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1632–1723) — The Delft Draper, Guarded Single-Bead Lenses, 'Little Animalcules,' and 50 Years of Royal Society Letters
item.description: How an unlettered Delft draper and municipal chamberlain who knew zero Latin taught himself to forge pinhead glass beads between hammered brass plates, stunned London's skeptical Royal Society with notarized Dutch affidavits proving millions of living bacteria swarmed inside a drop of pepper-water, locked his sharpest lenses away from Tsar Peter the Great and refused to train a single apprentice across fifty years of letters—before a post-chronology atomic descent inside the 219-chain Salmonella flagellar motor-hook complex (PDB 7CGO) reveals the 18,000 RPM proton-driven rotary engine that propelled his 1676 animalcules through water as thick as cold tar.

item.title: Isaac Newton (1642–1727) — Woolsthorpe's Plague Year, Secret Alchemy, the Principia Ambush, Hanging Counterfeiters at the Mint, and the Leibniz War
item.description: Follow the astonishing rise of Isaac Newton from a premature, fatherless Christmas Day 1642 orphan in Civil-War Lincolnshire who threatened to burn his hated stepfather's house down, emptied aristocrats' chamber pots at Trinity College, slid a darning bodkin behind his own living eyeball, and unlocked calculus, white light's spectrum, and the embryo of universal gravity during the solitary 1665–1666 Plague Year—yet locked almost all of it in his desk. Experience his bitter 1672 optics ambush by Robert Hooke, a million words of furnace-lit secret alchemy and career-risking Arian heresy, Edmond Halley's fateful August 1684 knock triggering an eighteen-month monastic sprint to forge the Principia Mathematica while scrubbing Hooke from its pages, his harrowing 1693 nervous collapse, and his shocking reinvention at the Tower of London—saving the Great Recoinage, running an undercover spy ring to hang master counterfeiter William Chaloner at Tyburn, accidentally placing Britain on the Gold Standard with his 1717 21-shilling guinea valuation, confiscating John Flamsteed's star catalog, secretly ghostwriting the Royal Society tribunal that broke Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz's heart, losing roughly 20,000 pounds sterling in the 1720 South Sea Bubble, and claiming a monarch's burial in Westminster Abbey.

item.title: Beyond Transitions: Prime Editing (PE6/PE7), Reversible ADAR RNA Editing & Suppressor ACE-tRNAs for Channelopathies — Prime Editing (8WUT/8WUV) for CFTR ΔF508 & transversions, reversible endogenous ADAR2 A→I editing (5ED1/6VFF), mutation-agnostic ACE-tRNAs for SCN1A/KCNJ13/CFTR nonsense rescue, and the biotech histories of Prime Medicine, Wave, Korro, Alltrna & Tevard
item.description: One-Ångström-Tall Man treatise walking inside Prime Editor initiation/elongation complexes (PDB 8WUT, 8WUV) and human ADAR2 monomer/asymmetric dimer dsRNA complexes (PDB 5ED1, 6VFF), engineering mechanics of epegRNAs, MLH1dn/MLH1-SB, PE6/PE7 La, AIMers/LEAPER 3.0, and ACE-tRNA PTC/NTC discrimination, plus two spoken calculation pauses and full biotech histories of Prime Medicine, Wave Life Sciences, Korro Bio, ProQR, Ascidian, Alltrna, and Tevard Biosciences.

item.title: From USD 150 Million Venture Philanthropy to a USD 10 Billion/Year Channel Empire: Vertex, the CF Foundation, the NaV1.7 Pain Graveyard & the Modern Ion-Channel Biotech Playbook — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside ΔF508 CFTR + Trikafta (8EIQ), NaV1.8 + A-803467 / VSD2 KKGS (7WE4), and Kv7.2 + retigabine (7CR2); Robert Beall's USD 150M-to-USD 3.3B Royalty Pharma triumph vs. the USD 1.5B NaV1.7 pain graveyard; Trikafta, Alyftrek, Journavx (suzetrigine), zorevunersen, relutrigine, azetukalner, opakalim (BHV-7000), and global pricing ethics
item.description: Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man biotech-history and cryo-EM structural pharmacology treatise contrasting the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation's USD 150M venture-philanthropy gamble (Aurora Biosciences USD 592M Vertex acquisition in 2001 -> USD 3.3B Royalty Pharma sale in Nov 2014 -> USD 11.02B 2024 and USD 12.0B 2025 Vertex CF empire across Kalydeco, Orkambi, Symdeko, Trikafta, and once-daily Alyftrek) against the USD 1.5B+ NaV1.7 pain graveyard (Pfizer PF-05089771, Biogen/Convergence vixotrigine USD 200M/USD 675M deal, Genentech/Xenon GDC-0276/GDC-0310, Amgen AMG 8379, Minett 2015 endogenous enkephalin/naloxone epistasis). Anchored to three verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures (8EIQ 3.0 Å ΔF508 CFTR + Trikafta/ATP/Mg2+, 7WE4 2.7 Å NaV1.8 + A-803467 & VSD2 KKGS crown, 7CR2 3.2 Å Kv7.2 + retigabine Trp236/Phe305 pocket), two explicit spoken Calculation Pauses (Venture-Philanthropy 22x / rNPV negative-to-positive flip; ΔΔG Boltzmann 130x dual-corrector folding multiplication & >95% occupancy cliff comparing PF-05089771 vs. suzetrigine), the 2020-2026 competitive landscape (Vertex Journavx Jan 2025 approval & Dec 2024 LSR placebo shock + VX-522 Moderna mRNA discontinuation; Stoke zorevunersen & Feb 2025 Biogen USD 165M deal; Praxis relutrigine/ulixacaltamide PDUFA dates; Xenon azetukalner X-TOLE2 & Sept 2026 NDA; Biohaven/SK Biopharm opakalim BHV-7000), and global pricing/access ethics (USD 370k WAC vs. Guo & Hill USD 5,676 generic API estimate and UK NICE July 2024 NHS agreement).

item.title: Crossing the Rare-Disease Valley of Death: The 1983 Orphan Drug Act, Priority Review Vouchers, AAV Safety Reckonings, n-Lorem & The Economics of Curing Ultra-Rare Channelopathies — One-Ångström walks inside ABE8e (PDB 6VPC), Prime Editor elongation complex (PDB 8WUV), and human NaV1.1/beta4 (PDB 7DTD); ultra-rare break-even rNPV & PRV sign-flip math + 1-to-3-quadrillion AAV hepatocyte MOI physics; Glybera, bluebird bio, Pfizer/Takeda/Vertex AAV exits, AT132 ASPIRO (NCT03199469), n-Lorem, NIH BGTC, FDA Platform Designation, ETX101 (NCT05419492) & Baby KJ 2025
item.description: Complete five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man biophysical, clinical, economic, and policy treatise confronting the Rare-Disease Valley of Death for ultra-rare channelopathies. Contrasts 1-Ångström molecular readiness against commercial collapses (uniQure Glybera 1-patient withdrawal, bluebird bio 3 FDA approvals yet >99% equity collapse to May 2025 Carlyle/SK Capital USD 45M buyout, and 2023-2025 Takeda/Pfizer Beqvez/Vertex/Novartis AAV pullbacks). Walks at 1 Å inside verified RCSB PDBs 6VPC (ABE8e TadA-8e Zn2+/Glu59/Val106/Asn108/Arg111/8AZ + SpCas9 D10A Ala207), 8WUV (2024 Prime Editor SpCas9 H840A + M-MLV RT YVDD Asp224/Asp225 + 2DA16-U109 Watson-Crick pairing showing 99% macromolecular invariance underpinning FDA Platform Technology Designation), and 7DTD (human NaV1.1/beta4 Cys919-Cys58, IFM latch Phe1499, pore Phe1774/9Z9 illustrating the 6.0-kb single-AAV limit, >1,800 private Dravet mutations, and Encoded Therapeutics' mutation-agnostic ETX101 NCT05419492). Includes two explicit spoken Calculation Pauses (ultra-rare break-even net/list price, risk-adjusted NPV = -USD 15.87M flipped to +USD 11.29M/+USD 16.73M by a USD 125M-150M PRV; and 10 kg infant systemic AAV vector load of 1-3 quadrillion vg reaching 60,000 vg / 120,000 capsids per hepatocyte at 3x10^14 vg/kg vs 100-fold reduction via engineered capsids). Covers the 1983 Orphan Drug Act, RPD PRVs (2024-2026 USD 150M-210M sales and Feb 3, 2026 reauthorization through Sept 30, 2029), AT132 ASPIRO cholestatic hepatotoxicity (NCT03199469, Karolczak JCI 2023), Zolgensma TMA/DRG/GLI1 safety, Stanley Crooke's n-Lorem Foundation (Cousin Med 2026), NIH AMP BGTC, FDA May 2024 Platform Technology Designation, and the landmark May 2025 CHOP/Penn/IGI/Aldevron/Acuitas Baby KJ 6-month LNP-ABE blueprint (Musunuru & Ahrens-Nicklas, NEJM 2025), closing with the next decisive extra-hepatic syncytial delivery shootout and Umbrella-CHAN platform trial roadmap.

item.title: Salt, Voltage, and the Silent Anion Gate: Endocrine Hypertension & Anion-Exchanger Channelopathies (KCNJ5, CLCN2, CACNA1D, Pendred & Congenital Chloride Diarrhea) — One-Ångström walks inside GIRK2/KCNJ5 (4KFM), human ClC-2 + AK-42 (8GQU), CaV1.3 EEEE/Gly403 (7UHG), and Pendrin (7WL7); adrenal GHK depolarization & ARR/AVS physics; mutant-selective macrolides, ABE9/PEmax & SLC26A4 ASO blueprints; and the USD 1.8 billion aldosterone synthase biotech saga (osilodrostat, baxdrostat, lorundrostat)
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_15 (Ep 2681): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, biophysical, base-editing, and biotech-history treatise covering endocrine hypertension channelopathies (KCNJ5/GIRK4 FH-III vs. somatic APA & G151E cell-death paradox; CLCN2 GoF FH-II vs. recessive CC2L leukoencephalopathy/chorioretinopathy/azoospermia; CACNA1D GoF PASNA vs. recessive exon-8B SANDD at Gly403) and sister SLC26 epithelial anion exchangers (SLC26A4 Pendred syndrome EVA/goiter/perchlorate discharge & SLC26A3 Congenital Chloride Diarrhea fecal Cl- > 90 mM with metabolic alkalosis). Anchored to verified RCSB PDB geometries 4KFM, 8GQU, 7UHG, and 7WL7; includes two spoken calculation pauses (zona glomerulosa GHK depolarization shifts; ARR/AVS lateralization, CLD stool Cl- flux, and empirical Phase 3 BaxHTN/Launch-HTN BP reductions); covers mutant-selective macrolides (MAPA), AK-42, codon-exact ABE9/PEmax/SLC26A4 c.919-2A>G ASO strategies, and the 20-year CYP11B2 vs. CYP11B1 ASI biotech history (Novartis/Recordati USD 390 million osilodrostat, CinCor/AstraZeneca USD 1.8 billion baxdrostat, Mineralys USD 192 million IPO lorundrostat).

item.title: Cilia, Slit Diaphragms, and Acidic Endosomes: PKD2 ADPKD, TRPC6 Podocyte FSGS & CLCN5 Dent Disease 1 — Mayo htTKV & PKD1 6-pseudogene traps, steroid-resistant TRPC6 FSGS & the calcineurin-synaptopodin paradox, Dent 1 CLCN5 vs. OCRL LMW proteinuria, 1-Å cryo-EM walks inside PKD2 (5T4D), TRPC6+AM-0883 (6UZ8) & CLC-7/OSTM1 (7JM7, Glu247=ClC-5 Glu211), endosomal V-ATPase stall & TEMPO/REPRISE economics, Otsuka Jynarque REMS, Novartis USD 1.7B Regulus farabursen buyout, Boehringer BI 764198 Lancet FSGS readout, and base/prime/CRISPRa editing across the glomerular filtration barrier
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_16 (Ep 2682): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, structural-biophysics, gene-editing, and biotech-history treatise uniting three specialized renal subcellular microdomains: (1) Primary-cilium PKD2 (TRPP2) / PKD1 ADPKD (Mayo Imaging Classification 1A-1E, 8-11% intracranial berry aneurysm MRA screening, PKD1 exons 1-33 6-pseudogene LR-PCR trap, Cornec-Le Gall median ESRD ages 55.6/67.9/79.7 yr, Outeda 2026 D511V VSD destabilization & Tian 2026 RASSF4 potentiation); (2) Podocyte slit-diaphragm dominant GoF TRPC6 FSGS (P112Q, M132T, R895C, E897K; steroid resistance & calcineurin-synaptopodin-cathepsin-L paradox; up to 14% monogenic adult FSGS); and (3) Proximal-tubule apical endosomal CLCN5 Dent Disease 1 vs. OCRL Dent Disease 2 (dipstick-albumin discordance, 100x-1000x urine beta-2-microglobulin/RBP, hypercalciuria, medullary nephrocalcinosis, rickets, 30-80% ESRD ages 30-50). Grounded in three verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures with 40+ measured interatomic distances: 5T4D (3.0 Å human PKD2 nanodisc: LGD selectivity filter Asp643-Arg638 2.67 Å, Gly642-Ile639 2.91 Å, S6 Leu677 hydrophobic gate 3.41 Å), 6UZ8 (2.84 Å human TRPC6 + agonist AM-0883 R0D + lipid SBM: FSGS brake contacts Arg895-Glu897 2.91 Å, Met132-Lys864 2.92 Å, Pro112-Glu900 3.47 Å, R0D-Trp680 3.32 Å, R0D-SBM lipid kiss 3.72 Å), and 7JM7 (2.82 Å human CLC-7/OSTM1 homolog of ClC-5: gating glutamate Glu247 [= ClC-5 Glu211] 2.98 Å from S_ext CL904, S_cen CL903-Tyr602 2.29 Å, S_int CL905-Gly203 2.77 Å, CBS ATP-Lys785 1.69 Å, ATP-Mg 1.96 Å, Mg-Glu95 2.43 Å, interfacial PI(3)P 0J1-Lys285 2.17 Å). Includes two fully worked spoken Calculation Pauses (300-nm endosome V-ATPase 318-ms stall at 3,177 H+ / +180 mV vs. 357,571 H+ buffered requirement and ClC-5 +42.0 mM luminal Cl- concentration; Mayo Class 1D htTKV doubling times & REPRISE 6.77 dialysis-free years vs. USD 280,000/yr Jynarque economics), full biotech histories (Otsuka tolvaptan TEMPO 3:4 / 2013 CRL / REPRISE / 2018 REMS; Regulus RGLS4326 clinical hold -> farabursen RGLS8429 Phase 1b 0.05% htTKV arrest -> Novartis 2025 USD 800M upfront / USD 1.7B CVR acquisition; Vertex VX-407 AGLOW; Boehringer Ingelheim BI 764198 COVID-19 ARDS Thorax 2023 failure -> Lancet 2026 FSGS 35% vs 7.1% / 44% at 20 mg & Phase 3 NCT07220083), ABE8e/CBE/iSTOP/Prime/CRISPRa strategies across the 6-8 nm glomerular filtration barrier, textbook myth debunking (Delling & Clapham 2016 cilia Ca2+, immune-FSGS dogma, Jentsch 2010 ClC-5 E211A uncoupling), and a decisive two-arm cryo-EM + porcine/NHP renal-delivery experiment.

item.title: The Upside-Down Metronome and the Stalled Wire: HCN1 DEE, HCN4 Familial Sick Sinus & IST, and TRPM4 Progressive Heart Block — SCN1A-Negative Dravet-Mimic HCN1 Cation-Leak DEE (M305L, G391D, D401H), HCN4 LoF Bradycardia/LVNC/AFib vs. R524Q Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia, TRPM4 E7K Impaired-DeSUMOylation Purkinje Depolarization Block, One-Ångström Walks Inside 5U6P/7NP4/6BQV, Phase-4 SA-Node & GHK Interneuron Calculations, Servier/Amgen Ivabradine (SHIFT vs. SIGNIFY & Phosphenes), Propofol-Site Stabilizers, ABE9/Prime Editing, and HCN2/TBX18 Biological Pacemakers
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_17 (Ep 2683): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, structural, and biotech treatise uniting three pacemaker and conduction channelopathies: (1) de novo HCN1 transmembrane cation-leak DEE (M305L, G391D, D401H) mimicking SCN1A Dravet syndrome with febrile status epilepticus and paradoxical phenytoin/lamotrigine exacerbation; (2) HCN4 bi-directional cardiac pacemaker disease contrasting autosomal-dominant LoF familial sinus bradycardia (34-42 bpm), LVNC, atrial fibrillation, and AV block against C-linker GoF R524Q cAMP-hypersensitive familial Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia; and (3) TRPM4 E7K (c.19G>A) autosomal-dominant Progressive Familial Heart Block Type IB (PFHB1B), where impaired deSUMOylation/endocytosis stacks 2-3x excess monovalent Na+-conducting TRPM4 channels on His-Purkinje fibers, depolarizing V_rest and driving NaV1.5 into steady-state inactivation (conduction block). Anchored at 1 Å inside three verified RCSB cryo-EM PDBs: 5U6P (3.51 Å human HCN1 + cAMP: S4 Arg267-Asn179 2.99 Å / Asp233 3.77 Å, flared CIGYG Cys358 3.09/3.26 Å vs. Tyr361 14.22 Å, S5 Met305-S6 Phe389 4.78 Å propofol/M305L clutch, S6 Val390 gate 3.62/3.79 Å, CNBD Arg549-cAMP 2.76 Å), 7NP4 (3.3 Å cAMP-bound rabbit HCN4 with explicit +1 residue mapping to human HCN4: CIGYG Ile480-Ser475 2.87 Å, outward S6 Phe510-Tyr507 3.12 Å / Met426 4.13 Å bracing the open-pore ivabradine cavity, CNBD Cys663-cAMP 2.54 Å and Arg670-cAMP 2.87 Å), and 6BQV (3.1 Å human TRPM4 + Ca2+ nanodisc: monovalent FGQIPQED filter Gln977 7.21 Å / Glu981 10.68 Å excluding Ca2+, Ile1040 3.72 Å & Tyr1045 S6 lower gate, S1-S4 Ca2+ pocket Gln831 2.27 Å and Glu828/Asn865/Asp868 2.66 Å). Includes two verified spoken calculation pauses (SA-node Phase-4 slope dV/dt = -I_net/C_m showing 70 -> 42 and 115 bpm balanced-current amplification; mixed Na+/K+ GHK E_rev at P_Na/P_K = 0.25 vs. 1.0 driving cortical PV+ interneuron NaV1.1 depolarization block), full Servier/Amgen ivabradine business & SHIFT (N=6,558) vs. SIGNIFY (N=19,102) clinical trial history plus retinal HCN1 phosphenes and mid-2024 generic entry, propofol-site non-anesthetic HCN1 stabilizers and Florey/Petrou Org 34167 & allele-specific ASO programs, concrete narrow-window ABE9 (TRPM4 E7K c.19G>A guarding c.20A bystander; HCN1 G391D; HCN4 R524Q), CBE (S399P), and Prime Editing (HCN1 M305L/D401H transversions) blueprints, and HCN2/TBX18 biological pacemakers vs. dual-chamber/LBBAP pacing.

item.title: Tunnels Between Worlds, Leaks That Kill: Gap-Junction & Leaky-Hemichannel Syndromes (GJB1/Cx32 CMTX1, GJB2 KID Syndrome, GJA1/Cx43 ODDD & PANX1 Oocyte Death) — Schwann-cell radial myelin shortcuts (1,414-fold path reduction across 50 wraps) and altitude/fever CNS stroke-like episodes in GJB1/Cx32 CMTX1 (5' UTR c.-17G>A trap & 852-bp intrathecal AAV9-Mpz-GJB1), toxic dominant GJB2 Asp50Asn/Gly45Glu leaky hemichannels vs. recessive 35delG deafness (abEC1.1 mAb & c.148A>G Adenine Base Editing), GJA1/Cx43 ODDD & GJA1-20k cardiac protection, and heptameric PANX1 gain-of-function human oocyte death rescued by probenecid (PDB 7ZXM, 7XQF, 6WBF, 2ZW3)
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_18 (Ep 2684): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, structural-biophysical, gene-editing, and venture-philanthropy treatise uniting four gap-junction and large-pore leaky-hemichannel syndromes: GJB1/Cx32 X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMTX1: 30-40 m/s intermediate MNCV, split-hand atrophy, transient altitude/fever CNS stroke-like splenium DWI lesions via Paulson 2002 CSF acidosis and panglial Cx32:Cx30/Cx47:Cx43 collapse, 5' UTR c.-17G>A & c.-17+1G>T sequencing trap, 852-bp single-AAV9-Mpz-GJB1 Schwann-cell therapy by Kleopa/Kagiava overcoming Golgi-retained R75W/N175D dominant-negative mutants, and CMTA-STAR/CMTRF/Armatus Bio translational economics), GJB2/Cx26 dominant KID syndrome (Asp50Asn c.148G>A & Gly45Glu c.134G>A constitutively leaky hemichannels causing deafness, erythrokeratoderma, vascularizing keratitis, IL15/CCL5/TLR5 downregulation, lethal sepsis, and >=12% early SCC vs. benign recessive 35delG DFNB1A deafness; hemichannel-selective human mAb abEC1.1 at IC50 ~40 nM and direct c.148A>G Adenine Base Editing), GJA1/Cx43 ODDD (Gly21Arg & Arg76His/Ser syndactyly, enamel hypoplasia, microcornea, adult spastic paraparesis, lipid-gated GCN/FIN/PLN equilibrium, and M213 GJA1-20k cardiac protection), and heptameric PANX1 gain-of-function Mendelian female infertility / oocyte death (Q392*, K346E, C347S aberrant glycosylation and ATP hemorrhage rescued ex vivo by probenecid/spironolactone). Grounded in four verified RCSB PDB structures (7ZXM 2.14 Å human Cx32, 2ZW3 3.5 Å human Cx26, 7XQF 2.3 Å human Cx43 nanodisc + C14 lipids, 6WBF 2.83 Å heptameric human PANX1 + Trp74/Arg75/DGA), two step-by-step spoken calculation pauses (Einstein-Smoluchowski 50-wrap Schwann spiral 1,414-fold path / ~20,000-to-2-million-fold diffusion time speedup; Cx26 D50N 100-300 open hemichannels driving Ca2+ toxicity in 2.6 s and 3 mM ATP bleed-out in under 60 s), all 17 dossier PMIDs, and verified ClinicalTrials.gov trials (NCT05902351, NCT07461896, NCT03124459, NCT05008874, NCT02699190, NCT05687474, NCT05982119).

item.title: Fast-Spiking Fire, Big Potassium & The Scalloped Iris: KCNC1 MEAK, KCNA2, KCNMA1 & ITPR1 — Paradoxical Fever Rescue in KCNC1 R320H MEAK & One-Guide ABE Editing, 4-Aminopyridine GoF vs. LoF Polarity in KCNA2 Encephalopathy, Alcohol/Caffeine-Triggered KCNMA1 D434G/N999S PNKD3 Rescued by Lisdexamfetamine vs. Liang-Wang Syndrome, ITPR1 Dominant-Negative Gillespie Scalloped Aniridia vs. SCA15 Haploinsufficiency, 15/16 Tetramer-Poisoning Math & Autifony Therapeutics (AUT00201 / AUT00206) Biotech History (PDB 8F1C, 7PQT, 6V3G, 7LHE)
item.description: 5-Act One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy, Base-Editor & Biotech History Treatise (Ep 2685) uniting four obligate homotetrameric cerebellar/myoclonus/BK channelopathies across four verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures: human Kv3.1 + positive allosteric modulator X9T/Compound 4 + K+ + Zn2+ + POV (PDB 8F1C, 2.92 Å, Chen et al., PNAS 2023, PMID 37812700), apo human Kv3.1 (PDB 7PQT, 2.65 Å, Botte et al., PNAS Nexus 2022, PMID 36741467), Ca2+-free human BK/Slo1 KCNMA1 (PDB 6V3G, 4.0 Å, Tao & MacKinnon, eLife 2019, PMID 31815672), and full-length tetrameric ER IP3R1 in lipid nanodisc with PLX & Zn2+ (PDB 7LHE, 3.3 Å, Baker et al., Commun Biol 2021). Covers four clinical cases & testing traps (MEAK KCNC1 p.Arg320His paradoxical fever improvement vs. seizure-free p.Arg339* NMD haploinsufficiency; KCNA2 LoF vs. GoF ClinVar polarity & Hedrich/Lerche 2021 4-AP rescue vs. Wu et al. 2026 SUDEP; KCNMA1 D434G/N999S alcohol/caffeine PNKD3 rescued by lisdexamfetamine vs. Liang-Wang LoF & Moldenhauer/Meredith 2024 KMS VUS score; ITPR1 Gillespie scalloped aniridia dominant-negative pore variants vs. SCA15 deletion haploinsufficiency & Romaniello 2022 83% superior cerebellar atrophy MRI clue), 35+ verified interatomic distances (Kv3.1 R4 ARG320–PHE256 2.84/3.10 Å, TLGYG filter, X9T–PRO373 2.14 Å & POV603 2.33 Å, T1 ZN601 2.30/1.93 Å; BK TVGYG, RCK1 ASP434–ASN465 2.42 Å, Ca2+ bowl ASP895; IP3R1 GGVGD GLY2547–ARG2544(D) 3.64 Å & ASP2551 3.94 Å, S6 gate LEU2582–PHE2586 3.06 Å, PLX 2.88 Å, C2H2 Zn2+ 1.71–2.32 Å), two spoken calculation pauses (15/16 binomial tetramer poisoning 6.25% vs. 50% haploinsufficiency vs. 40% ABE binary rescue 43.75%; PV+ fast-spiking interneuron repolarization t_repol 0.52 ms -> 2.08 ms & f_max 355 Hz -> 135 Hz -> 287 Hz PAM / 355 Hz ABE), single-guide ABE for KCNC1 c.959G>A and opposite-strand CBE for KCNMA1 c.1301A>G, KCIAF patient advocacy, and Autifony Therapeutics biotech history (2011 GSK spinout, QUIET-1 tinnitus futility, EUR 627.5M Boehringer deal & AUT00206 gamma/FDOPA biomarkers, 2020 returned rights, AUT00201 MEAK Ph1b NCT05873062 & USD 770.5M Jazz deal).

item.description: Wave 11 Flagship Episode CHAN_21 (Ep 2687): Complete five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man biophysical, clinical, and biotech-history treatise on DNA Base Editing for Ion Channelopathies. Explains why giant channel CDS (>4.7 kb AAV limit), dominant-negative tetramers, and post-mitotic DSB/HDR failure broke classical gene therapy and Cas9 nucleases; walks at 1 Å inside four verified experimental structures — PDB 6VPC (3.2 Å ABE8e + R-loop + 8AZ26 + Zn2+/Mg2+, explicitly noting SpCas9 D10A = Ala207 +197 offset, Glu59, Val106, Asn108, and 590–1,100-fold kinetic turbocharger T111R Arg111 at 2.33 Å), PDB 8E2P (2.72 Å TadA*8.20 + ssDNA UEL9 showing the 2.70 Å hairpin U-turn behind the 4–8 editing window and CBE-T evolution), PDB 5SWW (3.151 Å human APOBEC3A E72A trapped + ssDNA + Zn2+ + UGI biology), and PDB 8E5E (2.62 Å bacterial toxin DddA E1347A + dsDNA tandem base-displacement unlocking CRISPR-free mitochondrial DdCBE and TALED editing); dissects all Five Unique Channelopathy Base-Editing Strategies (Direct Reversion for SCN8A R1872W, TMC1 Baringo c.545A>G, KCNC1 R320H, CFTR R553X/R1162X/W1282X; PAM-flexible SpG/SpRY & narrow-window V106W/ABE9/YE1/CBE-T/OpenABE bystander shielding; BE-SKIP splice disruption for CACNA1C Timothy exon 8A; allele-specific iSTOP silencing for dominant GoF RYR2/KCNT1/CLCN7; and Split-Intein Dual-AAV vs. eVLP vs. GalNAc-LNP/PNP delivery); includes two spoken Calculation Pauses (Dual-AAV packaging budget & Poisson co-transduction at MOI = 2 vs. MOI = 5; bystander purity ABE8e vs. ABE9 & homotetramer w^4 vs. monomeric editing thresholds); traces David Liu lab -> Beam Therapeutics (2017 founding, 2020 IPO, Pfizer USD 1.35B deal, Lilly USD 600M Verve opt-in buyout, BEAM-101 BEACON pivotal Nov 2026 & BEAM-302 18-month AATD readouts) -> Verve Therapeutics (VERVE-101 Apr 2024 LNP pause -> VERVE-102 GalNAc-LNP NEJM 2026 -> Eli Lilly USD 1.3B 2025 acquisition) and the Broad vs. CVC Cas9 + Beam deaminase IP royalty stack; debunks base-editing myths and designs the decisive post-onset SCN8A structural and in vivo experiment.

item.title: Joseph Priestley & Carl Wilhelm Scheele (1733–1804 / 1742–1786) — Fire-Air, the Burning Lens, the Taste of Cyanide, and the Birmingham Riots
item.description: How a Yorkshire Dissenter beside a Leeds brewery and a freezing Swedish apothecary using pig bladders unlocked oxygen, chlorine, soda water, and ten new gases—only for slow printers, a candid Paris dinner, heavy-metal poisons, and a Bastille Day mob to cost them priority, health, and home.

item.title: Antoine-Laurent & Marie-Anne Lavoisier (1743–1794 / 1758–1836) — Tax-Farming Capital, Oxygen, 13 Copperplates, and the Widow's Revenge
item.description: How a Parisian tax-farmer and his brilliant thirteen-year-old bride armed the American Revolution with gunpowder, proved respiration is combustion, shattered Aristotle's four elements, engraved the bible of modern chemistry—and collided fatally with Jean-Paul Marat and the Reign of Terror.

item.title: John Dalton & Amedeo Avogadro (1766–1844 / 1776–1856) — Atomic Weights, the HO Trap, Diatomic Molecules, and Cannizzaro's Pamphlet
item.description: How a color-blind Cumberland Quaker schoolmaster weighed invisible atoms yet choked on water's formula, why a quiet Turin lawyer's 1811 diatomic solution was ignored for fifty years of chemical anarchy, and how a Sicilian revolutionary's pamphlet at Karlsruhe made the scales fall from Europe's eyes.

item.title: Robert Boyle & Robert Hooke (1627–1691 / 1635–1703) — The Earl's Son, the Orphan Mechanic, the Air-Pump, Micrographia, Phosphorus, and Newton's Wrath
item.description: How Ireland's richest aristocratic prodigy and a crooked-spined Isle of Wight servitor forged the pneumatic air-pump, Boyle's Law, modern chemistry, the biological cell, and London's post-fire skyline—before alchemy, cold urine-distilled phosphorus, and Isaac Newton's fury tore their legacies apart.

item.title: Michael Faraday (1791–1867) — 386 Bound Pages, the First Motor, Electrolysis Laws, Magnetized Light, and Lines of Force
item.description: How a Southwark blacksmith's son armed with one loaf of bread a week and zero university calculus rose from bookbinding to liquefy gases, isolate benzene, invent the electric motor and dynamo, quantize electrolysis, twist light with a magnet, refuse knighthood, and hand James Clerk Maxwell the invisible field universe.

item.title: Jöns Jacob Berzelius & Friedrich Wöhler (1779–1848 / 1800–1882) — The Chemical Alphabet, Isomerism, Protein, and Göttingen's 8,000 Chemists
item.description: How a Swedish orphan working beside his housekeeper's soup stove weighed 2,000 compounds, invented modern H₂O notation, and coined isomerism, catalysis, and protein—while his adopted German protégé synthesized biological urea from inorganic salts, united with rival Justus Liebig on bitter almonds, and trained 8,000 chemists across two continents.

item.title: Dmitri Mendeleev (1834–1907) — The 1,400-Mile Siberian Carriage, Chemical Solitaire, Gallium's Density Correction, Bigamy, and the 1906 One-Vote Nobel Snub
item.description: How a Siberian glassmaker's youngest son rode 1,400 miles across the Urals on his dying mother's last rubles, missed a cheese-dairy train to play solitaire with 63 element cards, boldly corrected a French discoverer's lab measurement from 1,500 miles away, survived Tsarist blackballing, and lost the 1906 Nobel Prize by one vindictive Stockholm vote.

item.title: Svante Arrhenius & Josiah Willard Gibbs (1859–1927 / 1839–1903) — Gibbs Free Energy, the 4th-Class Thesis, the 1896 CO₂ Calculation, and the Nobel Gatekeeper
item.description: How an unpaid New Haven bachelor wrote the thermodynamic bible of chemistry inside an unread Connecticut journal while a brash Swedish rebel nearly flunked his PhD over dissolved salt ions—then rallied Europe's young Ionists, hand-calculated CO₂ global warming in 1896, won the 1903 Chemistry Nobel, and turned Stockholm's Nobel committees into his personal fortress.

item.title: Marie Skłodowska Curie & Ernest Rutherford (1867–1934 / 1871–1937) — The Flying University, Pitchblende Cauldrons, Gold Foil, Two Nobels, and Splitting the Atom
item.description: How a Polish governess from Warsaw's secret Flying University boiled tons of Bohemian ore to isolate polonium and radium and survived Paris's xenophobic mobs to claim two Nobel Prizes—while a booming New Zealand farmboy proved radioactivity is atomic transmutation, bounced alpha shells off gold foil to reveal the atomic nucleus, and artificially split nitrogen.

item.title: Gilbert N. Lewis, Fritz Haber & R.B. Woodward (1875–1946 / 1868–1934 / 1917–1979) — Haber-Bosch, Ypres, the Covalent Bond, 41 Nobel Snubs, Vitamin B₁₂, and Orbital Symmetry
item.description: How Fritz Haber conjured 'bread from air' only to unleash chlorine gas at Ypres and perish exiled by the Nazis; how Gilbert N. Lewis invented the shared-electron-pair bond, Lewis acids, and heavy water yet died amid HCN fumes after 41 Nobel snubs; and how MIT flunk-out R.B. Woodward turned strychnine, chlorophyll, Vitamin B₁₂, and orbital symmetry into high architectural art.

item.title: Linus Pauling (1901–1994) — The Chemical Bond, α-Helix, DNA Race, and Two Unshared Nobels
item.description: Strictly chronological 4-Act progression. Do not spoil the Nobels, DNA blunder, or Vitamin C controversy in earlier Acts; examine dispassionately how supreme intuition yields both revolutionary leaps and late-career blind spots.

item.title: Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin (1910–1994) — Penicillin, Vitamin B12, Insulin, and Quiet Iron
item.description: Strictly chronological 4-Act progression. Do NOT spoil Margaret Roberts becoming Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher during Act 2, nor spoil insulin's 1969 conquest or the 1964 Nobel in earlier Acts; highlight her ego-free, velvet-over-diamond institutional mastery.

item.title: Werner Forssmann's 1929 Self-Catheterization & Andreas Grüntzig's Kitchen-Table Balloon Angioplasty — Eberswalde 1929: strapping nurse Gerda Ditzen onto the table to thread a 65-cm ureteral catheter into his own right atrium, Sauerbruch's 'circus' firing, Cournand & Richards's 1956 Nobel revival, Mason Sones's 1958 accidental coronary angiogram ('Cough!'), Andreas Grüntzig's Zurich kitchen-table PVC balloon on Adolf Bachmann (Sept 16, 1977), RAVEL (0.0% restenosis) & CURE DAPT inside FKBP12–sirolimus–mTOR FRB, P2Y12 & aspirin-COX (PDB 1FAP, 4NTJ, 4PXZ, 5F19)

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (I): The Scintillation Counter & the Fluid Membrane — Paul D. Ray, Art Spector & Docosahexaenoic Acid (1929–1989)
item.description: Episode I of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants legacy series honoring American biochemist Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): from Bemidji State University (B.S. 1976; Outstanding Alumni Award 2003) and isolated perfused rabbit livers with Ph.D. mentor Paul D. Ray at the University of North Dakota (lineage of Nobel Laureate Edward A. Doisy and Henry A. Lardy) to postdoctoral work at Iowa with NIH-trained lipid pioneer Arthur A. Spector, culminating in the 1,501-citation classic Spector & Yorek (1985, J. Lipid Res.) proving how 22:6n-3 (DHA) remodels membrane fluidity, Eadie-Hofstee high-affinity neurotransmitter uptake, and receptor signaling.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (II): The Sugar Decoy & the Sodium Pump — Myo-Inositol, SMIT & the L-Fucose Breakthrough (1973–1998)
item.description: Episode II of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: how Gabbay (1973) and Greene, Lattimer & Sima (1987, NEJM) framed the polyol-myo-inositol-Na+/K+-ATPase hypothesis of diabetic neuropathy, why human aldose reductase inhibitor trials faltered, and how Mark Yorek, Joyce A. Dunlap, and Lawrence J. Coppey used 3H-myo-inositol, ouabain-sensitive 86Rb+/22Na+ pump flux, Northern blots of SMIT mRNA, and the deceptive hexose L-fucose (J. Neurochem., JBC, Diabetes 1987–1998) to prove competitive transport inhibition, rescue nerve conduction velocity in diabetic rats, and discover why endothelial cells refused to behave like pure nerves.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (III): Hanging the 60-Micron Vessel — Epineurial Arterioles & Why Nerves Starve Before They Die (1980–2006)
item.description: Episode III of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: building on Furchgott & Zawadzki (1980), Tuck, Schmelzer & Low (1984), and Peter J. Dyck (1985), Mark Yorek, Lawrence J. Coppey, Jill S. Gellett, Eric P. Davidson, and Donald D.istad/Heistad perfected pressurized videomicroscopy of 60–100 micron sciatic epineurial arterioles—proving via Poiseuille's r^4 law, laser Doppler endoneurial blood flow, acetylcholine (NO + EDHF) vs CGRP relaxation, and temporal time-course studies (Diabetes 2000–2003) that microvascular endothelial dysfunction precedes motor nerve conduction slowing.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (VI): Forty Years Back to Omega-3 — Resolvin D1, Nerve Regeneration & Horizons to 2050
item.description: Episode VI (Grand Finale) of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): how the 1983–1985 DHA neural lipid discoveries with Art Spector came full circle 30–40 years later when Mark Yorek, Lawrence Coppey, Eric Davidson, Alexander Obrosov, and Matthew S. Yorek proved that omega-3 menhaden oil, 15-lipoxygenase-1 metabolites (Resolvin D1 / E1, neuroprotectin D1), and salsalate acetylation synergy don't merely slow diabetic neuropathy—they actively regenerate vanished corneal and intraepidermal nerve fibers, protect disuse skeletal muscle atrophy (2025, PMC12747565), establish rational combination therapy (2024–2025, PMC11133577, PMC12292556, PMC12341837), and inspire the 2026–2050 precision neurovascular regeneration era.

item.title: The Enzyme That Ran Out of Time — Chlorpyrifos/Paraoxon Phosphorylated Human AChE vs. Aged Dealkylated Adduct (PDB 5HF5 / 5HF6 / 5HFA), Pralidoxime Reactivation Window, RBC vs. Plasma Cholinesterase & Eddleston RCT
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 113: Chlorpyrifos/Paraoxon Phosphorylated Human AChE vs. Aged Dealkylated Adduct (PDB 5HF5 / 5HF6 / 5HFA), Pralidoxime Reactivation Window, RBC vs. Plasma Cholinesterase & Eddleston RCT. In the emergency department, suction clears the airway and the cardiac rate rises. Hours later, the person still cannot sustain ventilation. The Critical Care Clinician follows breathing, perfusion and strength. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows a phosphorus atom from a pesticide oxon to a covalent bond on acetylcholinesterase, then asks what makes that bond harder to undo. The patient, dialogue and individual measurements are fictional. Chapter 132, “Acetylcholinesterase and its Inhibitors,” in the live Pharmacology notebook’s *Primer on the Autonomic Nervous System* (2012), names parathion and discusses paraoxon, inhibition and aging. The clinical case concerns a different diethyl pesticide, chlorpyrifos. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Ring That Reversed Paralysis — Rocuronium at Adult Human Muscle nAChR (PDB 9DMH), Modified Gamma-Cyclodextrin Sugammadex Host–Guest Encapsulation, Quantitative Train-of-Four Recovery & Recurarization Physics
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 98: Rocuronium at Adult Human Muscle nAChR (PDB 9DMH), Modified Gamma-Cyclodextrin Sugammadex Host–Guest Encapsulation, Quantitative Train-of-Four Recovery & Recurarization Physics. The operation is over. The anesthesiologist sees four responses on the monitor, but the last one is still small. The Critical Care Clinician follows recovery from rocuronium through the numbers on the screen. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows two encounters with the same steroid, first at a muscle receptor and then inside a synthetic sugar ring. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. Chapter 33, “Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors,” in the Pharmacology notebook’s Handbook of Cell Signaling, second edition (2010), introduces muscle-type postsynaptic receptors and their gating states. Primary studies supply the rocuronium and sugammadex evidence. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Drug That Changed What HLA Shows — Abacavir F-Pocket Remodeling of HLA-B*57:01 Self-Peptide Repertoire (PDB 3VRI), PREDICT-1 Prospective Screening & Patch-Test-Confirmed vs. Clinical Hypersensitivity
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 94: Abacavir F-Pocket Remodeling of HLA-B*57:01 Self-Peptide Repertoire (PDB 3VRI), PREDICT-1 Prospective Screening & Patch-Test-Confirmed vs. Clinical Hypersensitivity. Nine days after switching to an abacavir-containing HIV regimen, a woman arrives with fever, rash and gastrointestinal symptoms. Her pretreatment genetic report was negative. The Critical Care Clinician asks what that result can establish once a patient is ill. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows abacavir into two different molecular systems, the viral polymerase and the human peptide-presenting complex. The case, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is chapter 20, Adverse Drug Reactions, in the 2014 Handbook of Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine, section 20.4.3.1 on abacavir hypersensitivity. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Sedative and the Rising Lactate — Propofol Emulsion Discovery, GABAA Beta+/Alpha- Transmembrane Pocket (PDB 6X3T), Propofol-Related Infusion Syndrome (PRIS) Mitochondrial Acylcarnitine/CoQ Impairment & Brugada ECG

The arterial pressure trace narrows as a sedated trauma patient’s lactate rises. The Critical Care Clinician follows the change from a stable infusion to shock. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows propofol from an anesthesia patent into a neuronal receptor and then into a separate experiment on muscle mitochondria. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook’s “VOLUME XIII Anesthetic Crises and Perioperative Collapse” provides the propofol induction context. Primary sources supply the drug and infusion-syndrome evidence. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Channel That Opened Longer — CFTR G551D Open-Probability Defect, Ivacaftor (VX-770) Transmembrane Lasso/TM8 Hinge Binding (PDB 6O2P), STRIVE Sweat-Chloride vs. FEV1 Readouts & CFF Biomarker Interpretation

item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
item.description: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

item.title: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
item.description: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.

item.title: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
item.description: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

item.title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
item.description: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

item.title: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
item.description: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

item.title: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
item.description: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

item.title: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
item.description: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
item.description: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Pocket That Did Not Predict the Trial — Fragile X FMR1 Methylation PCR, Grm5 Rescue, Mavoglurant in Human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9), [11C]ABP688 PET & FXLEARN
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 79: FMR1 CGG repeat-primed and HpaII methylation PCR (Chen et al.), Fmr1 x Grm5 genetic cross (Dölen et al. 2007) and CTEP chronic rescue (Michalon et al. 2012), mavoglurant (AFQ056) bound 8 Å below the membrane surface in human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9, Asn747/Ser805/Ser809), human [11C]ABP688 PET receptor occupancy, why Jacquemont's (2011) 7-person full-methylation subgroup failed prospective replication in Phase 2b (Berry-Kravis et al. 2016), and the FXLEARN pediatric language trial (log10 contrast -0.10, P=.16).

item.title: The Signal That Tested the Pituitary — Ghrelin & GOAT Discovery, Macimorelin Bound to Human GHSR–Gq (PDB 9V2N), 22-kDa GH Immunoassay & ITT Crossover Agreement
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 78: reverse pharmacology from GHSR1a cloning (Howard et al. 1996) to rat stomach ghrelin isolation (Kojima et al. 1999) and GOAT/MBOAT4 Ser3 octanoylation (Yang 2008; Gutierrez 2008), peptidomimetic macimorelin (JMV1843) bound to human GHSR-Gq at 2.63 Å (PDB 9V2N, Asp99/Arg102/Ser123), 22-kDa IDS-iSYS chemiluminescent GH assay, thorough QTcF crossover (+9.61 ms at 4 h), and 139-pair vs. 140-pair diagnostic agreement against the insulin tolerance test (Garcia et al.).

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
item.description: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

item.title: The Protein That Met Resistance — Mouse 2×2 Dietary Amino Acid & Progressive Weight-Pulling Factorial (Trautman 2023), Sestrin2–Leucine Pocket & GATOR2 Cryo-EM vs. Longland & Layman Human Trials
item.description: Separating body-composition compartments, individual muscle hypertrophy, and glycemic tolerance when dietary protein meets resistance load: Trautman et al.'s (2023) 2x2 mouse amino-acid/weight-pulling factorial (protecting against fat accretion while leaving high-protein glucose intolerance unchanged, P=0.7442), Sestrin2–leucine and GATOR2 structural mechanics, Drummond's human rapamycin biopsy tracer study, and Longland (2016) vs. Layman (2005) human trials.

item.title: The Iron Test Before the School Bell — Non-Anemic Adolescent Iron Deficiency (TSAT 9.5%, Ferritin 10 µg/L), Human Ferroportin–Hepcidin Cryo-EM (6WBV), Alternate-Day Isotope Absorption & Thai vs. Baltimore School Trials
item.description: Separating storage biomarkers from classroom endpoints in iron deficiency without anemia: assay reference intervals vs. WHO/2026 AAP ferritin thresholds, human ferroportin–hepcidin cryo-EM occlusion and Co2+/Fe2+-coupled binding (PDB 6WBV, Kd 210 -> 2.5 nM), Stoffel's erythrocyte stable-isotope absorption trial (16.3% daily vs. 21.8% alternate-day), and Sungthong's Thai school trial (n=397) vs. Bruner's Baltimore verbal-learning RCT (n=81).

item.title: Three Sodium Levels, Two Diets, One Blood Pressure — Controlled DASH-Sodium Feeding Trial (n=412, −8.9 mmHg Path), 24-Hour Urinary Excretion, Human NCC–Hydrochlorothiazide Cryo-EM (9BWT), Urinary Vesicles & GWAS Limits
item.description: Controlled feeding trials meet distal-tubule atomic physiology: Sacks et al.'s (2001) DASH-Sodium parallel-diet/crossover-salt design (n=412, why non-additive interaction yields -8.9 mmHg rather than -12.6 mmHg), energy-scaled sodium density vs. 24h urine potentiometry, human phosphorylated NCC and hydrochlorothiazide cryo-EM (PDB 9BWT), KCl urinary extracellular vesicle readouts, and UK Biobank/CHARGE MTHFS gene-diet slope limits.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: The Fat That Never Got Digested — Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, Fecal Elastase CELA3A/3B ELISA vs. 72-Hour Fat Balance, Lipase-Colipase Lid Opening (1LPB) & Enteric Pancrelipase Trials
item.description: From watery-stool dilution artifacts in fecal elastase testing and Tóth's discovery that 'elastase-1' monoclonals actually measure CELA3B/CELA3A to 72-hour coefficient of fat absorption (CFA) balance math, Egloff's human pancreatic lipase-colipase open-lid crystal structure (PDB 1LPB), enteric-coated pancrelipase pH release kinetics, Whitcomb's 54-patient randomized trial, and fibrosing colonopathy incidence.

item.title: The Fructose That Locked Up Phosphate — Hereditary Fructose Intolerance, KHK Fructose-1-Phosphate Trapping vs. ALDOB A149P/A174D Crystal Structures, 31P-MRS Hepatic PME & KHK Inhibition
item.description: From infant post-weaning hypoglycemia, hypophosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and proximal renal Fanconi syndrome in Hereditary Fructose Intolerance to KHK-driven fructose-1-phosphate sequestration, human ALDOB A149P/A174D crystal structures, hepatic 31P-MRS phosphomonoester dynamics, and investigational ketohexokinase inhibition.

item.title: The Kidney After the Heat — Collecting-Duct AVP–V2R Cryo-EM (7DW9), AQP2 Ser256 Trafficking, Recurrent Rat Fructose Dehydration vs. Human Exercise Heat Crossovers
item.description: Separating physiological water conservation from tubular injury during heat stress and sweetened rehydration: human arginine vasopressin-V2R-Gs cryo-EM structure (PDB 7DW9) and PKA-driven AQP2 apical exocytosis, Chapman et al. (2020) 12-human heat-exercise soft-drink crossover, García-Arroyo et al. (2017) Wistar rat V1a/V2 conivaptan blockade, and Tourula et al. (2026) hypotonic vs. hypertonic sports drinks.

item.title: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
item.description: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
item.description: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

item.title: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
item.description: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

item.title: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
item.description: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
item.description: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

item.title: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
item.description: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

item.title: The Carbon in the Next Breath — [U-13C6]Fructose Meal Oxidation, KHK-A 2HW1 Active Site, GC-C-IRMS Plasma Glucose & 7T Hepatic Deuterium Imaging
item.description: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

item.title: One Ångström Under the Mucus — Human Airway Axonemal Dynein (PDB 8J07), Periciliary Brush Exclusion, DNAH5 Splice Defects & Nasal Nitric Oxide
item.description: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

item.title: One Ångström When the Artery Opens — Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion, Succinate Accumulation, Complex I Reverse Electron Transport & Infarct Salvage
item.description: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

item.title: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
item.description: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

item.title: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
item.description: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

item.title: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
item.description: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

item.title: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
item.description: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

item.title: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
item.description: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

item.title: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
item.description: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

item.title: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
item.description: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

item.title: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
item.description: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.
